claim: The generic thermal sysfs interface exposes thermal zones under /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone[0-*] with attributes type, temp (millidegrees Celsius), mode, policy, available_policies, trip_point_[0-*]_temp/_type/_hyst, emul_temp, and PID tuning attributes (sustainable_power, k_po, k_pu, k_i, k_d, integral_cutoff, slope, offset).
stance_target: agent thermal telemetry has a documented, stable sysfs contract including trip points for threshold alerting
scope_conditions: Linux kernel generic thermal sysfs driver; zone/cdev presence depends on registered drivers
quoted_support: /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone[0-*]: |---type: Type of the thermal zone |---temp: Current temperature |---mode: Working mode of the thermal zone |---policy: Thermal governor used for this zone |---available_policies: Available thermal governors for this zone |---trip_point_[0-*]_temp: Trip point temperature
time_period: kernel docs current for 7.3.0-rc1 (document written 2008, maintained)

claim: Thermal cooling devices expose cur_state/max_state and statistics under /sys/class/thermal/cooling_device[0-*]/stats/ (time_in_state_ms, total_trans, trans_table), and zone-to-cooler binding is visible via cdev[0-*], cdev[0-*]_trip_point and cdev[0-*]_weight attributes.
stance_target: agent can report fan/throttle state and even cooling statistics without proprietary tooling
scope_conditions: Linux generic thermal sysfs; cooling devices registered (fan, processor)
quoted_support: /sys/class/thermal/cooling_device[0-*]: |---type: Type of the cooling device(processor/fan/...) |---max_state: Maximum cooling state of the cooling device |---cur_state: Current cooling state of the cooling device |---stats: Directory containing cooling device's statistics |---stats/time_in_state_ms: Time (msec) spent in various cooling states

claim: On a critical thermal trip point crossing, the kernel thermal framework itself triggers an orderly hardware-protection power-off or reboot, escalating to forced power-off and then emergency_restart() — so the kernel will shut the machine down before any userspace agent can react at critical temperature.
stance_target: agent thermal alerting must be positioned as early-warning well below critical thresholds, since the kernel owns the critical shutdown path
scope_conditions: Linux thermal framework; critical trip point configured by platform firmware/DT
quoted_support: On an event of critical trip temperature crossing, the thermal framework will trigger a hardware protection power-off (shutdown) or reboot, depending on configuration. At first, the kernel will attempt an orderly power-off or reboot, but accepts a delay after which it proceeds to do a forced power-off or reboot, respectively. If this fails, emergency_restart() is invoked as last resort.

claim: A worked example in the thermal sysfs doc shows acpitz zone values of temp 37000 (37°C), trip points at 100000 critical / 80000 passive / 70000 active0 / 60000 active1, and an hwmon mirror (temp1_input 37000, temp1_crit 100000).
stance_target: illustrates the millidegree-Celsius scale and hwmon mirroring that an agent parser must handle
